A flaw in Drupal's installer (CVE-2026-132165) is being used against live sites. Under certain conditions, an attacker with no login can reinstall Drupal and take over the site or run code.

• Patched Nov 18. Exploited Nov 19, per Drupal

2. Xen Orchestra has an actively exploited auth bypass (CVE-2026-133469) that hands attackers admin, and potentially root on your XCP-ng hosts. Get to 6.9.2 or 6.10.1 and keep XO off the internet.

3. CISA also added five Mitel MiCollab flaws and a Juniper Session Smart Router bug to KEV yesterday. If either sits in your estate, that's today's patch job.

4. Microsoft confirms November updates can break NTLM auth through some third-party proxies, SSO and app packaging tools. It's part of a fix for a nasty RPC bug, so don't roll back; test those kit paths and watch for the fix.

5. 1Password says an employee's GitHub account was compromised, leading to names, emails and account metadata being taken. Vaults weren't touched. Nothing to change, but expect convincing phishing about invites and account recovery.

6. FIFA confirms personal and business data was stolen. A group calling itself Handsome Boy Hacking Club claims it took 12GB from FIFA's Microsoft environment. Good week to check how your helpdesk verifies who's calling.

7. Bitdefender found SYS010: Meta ads for free wallpaper apps that sneak in browser extensions to steal cookies, read email and even delete security alerts. Lock down extension installs by policy.

8. Eclypsium says 33 of 38 recent exploited-flaw advisories for network kit were in bundled parts like PHP, Node. js and OpenSSH. Ask your vendors how fast they ship upstream fixes.

9. Italian and Swiss cyber agencies warn of AI agents running attacks on critical infrastructure, chaining small misconfigs into full breaches within hours. Less on the internet means less to chain.

10. The NCSC says agentic attack tools exploit the same old weaknesses, just faster. Its advice: know your internet-facing assets, clear exposed credentials, fix misconfigs and protect your APIs.

If you use Google Chrome, take a few seconds today to check your settings and trigger an update. Google just rushed out an emergency fix for a critical sandbox escape vulnerability.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-134401, stems from improper input validation in the Chrome Variations component. A remote attacker could trick you into visiting a crafted webpage, bypass the browser sandbox completely, and run arbitrary code to grab your local files or sensitive data.

Google rolled out desktop versions 158.0.8127.88 and 89 across Windows, macOS, and Linux to seal the hole. Browsers usually wait for a full restart to apply patches, so it is genuinely worth bouncing the app manually before browsing anything suspicious.

Palo Alto Networks released PAN-OS fixes for CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia), a Linux kernel local privilege-escalation bug in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. Observed attacks chained it with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) against internet-exposed management interfaces. The only known path on PAN-OS starts with unauthenticated RCE via the management interface, then escalates to root with Fragnesia. Devices already on a PHP2Shell-fixed build are protected against the observed chain; the new builds close the kernel issue itself. CISA previously added the kernel bug to KEV.

If your firewall or management plane is reachable from the internet, treat it as urgent: restrict management to a dedicated network or jump host with MFA, confirm you are on a fixed build for your PAN-OS line, and review logs for unexpected PHP workers or webshells.

Three exposed directories contained evidence of an active intrusion crew’s operations. A large US hospital system’s material included staff credentials, 8,460 email addresses, an authentication dump, a web-server `phpinfo` capture, and a separately recorded VPN session. The records do not prove a successful domain login, patient-data loss, or continuous VPN access. A US manufacturer’s Azure blob container was enumerated using a live SAS token, yielding 155,568 object names, including QuickBooks files; the files indicate listing, not downloading. The crew also ran the manufacturer’s Windows hashes against a custom wordlist.

The toolkit included FortiGate credential checking and a probe for the FortiOS LDAP empty-password bypass CVE-2026-22153, plus scripts for Exchange MRSProxy pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-62911), TightVNC (CVE-2024-42049), and an LFI vulnerability (CVE-2026-87902). Other available tools included Impacket, Responder, PetitPotam, krbrelayx, PKINITtools, mitm6, and NetExec. Their presence does not establish successful use against named targets.

A malicious Java JDBC provider, `https://t.co/ls1A1701Aa.sqlserver.jdbc.TlsChannelFix`, runs code when loaded. A separate launcher XOR-decodes a file and starts a 2.1 MB Windows executable with components consistent with an Apollo-derived payload. A 7.7 MB Linux ELF was identified as a Poseidon implant. The crew also used custom Java HTTPS beaconing and clients for Net Monitor for Employees Professional over authenticated SOCKS relays. Reconnaissance output was base64-encoded and exfiltrated in chunks through HTTP GET request paths.

The files also contained 35,601 Kerberos key records across 11,867 principals from a Bangladeshi university and staged domain database and registry hives from a Swiss tax office. Hundreds of US law firms and several federal agencies were enumerated, but these are targets, not confirmed compromises. Credential-stuffing and exploit attempts against one law firm showed failures. A decoded Linux payload configuration and host mapping associated `https://t.co/hV4CvIqYGk` with `45.83.182.68`; a Mythic-labelled service was observed on port 7443, though attribution and current infrastructure ownership remain unconfirmed.

The gesture: open the rule governing access to vCenter. Check whether it allows connections from networks that do not need access.

The campaign exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, with an operator adapting public proofs of concept on the day they appeared. The custom exploit reportedly worked against default PHP/Apache configurations: a multipart POST with more than 1,000 fields and excessive header lines exhausted PHP’s memory limit, while a second request on the same keep-alive connection used residual session state to leak memory and invoke `system`. The exploit supported PHP builds through per-version calibration, but patched releases stopped the chain. The reported fixes are PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12.

The operator fingerprinted PHP/Apache hosts using Shodan, narrowing a pool of 68,198 hosts to a shortlist of about 5,042. The campaign targeted 595 unique IPs across 57 countries; 404 hosts were assessed as compromised, with approximately 290,000 files (9.5 GB) collected. Exploitation and collection were organized through a job-based C2 and an AI-agent system: a custom queue dispatched 39 workers backed by two self-hosted DeepSeek endpoints. The evidence indicates human-directed, AI-assisted operations; complete autonomous execution was not established.

Post-compromise activity included reverse shells, SSH-key installation, periodic beacons, token-protected PHP webshells, cron persistence, and localhost-only Dropbear tunnels. Collection scripts inventoried hosts, searched repositories for secrets, gathered database backups and application data, and harvested cloud credentials, OAuth tokens, session files, and source code. Stolen credentials enabled cloud enumeration and further access attempts. A separate financial-fraud effort reached withdrawal and account-takeover capabilities, but no cryptocurrency theft was confirmed; an unauthenticated Redis instance did yield about 3.3 million user records.

Defenders should investigate suspicious high-volume multipart PHP requests followed by a same-connection request, web-server processes spawning shells or download tools, new SSH keys, unauthorized PHP prepend directives, Dropbear on loopback, and outbound traffic to the reported C2 on port 8088 or reverse-shell ports 41000–49153. Patching alone is insufficient after compromise: affected hosts require investigation or reimaging, and exposed credentials should be rotated. The report does not attribute the activity to a known threat group.

An attacker patched a vulnerability on its own relay server. That is the detail I keep coming back to in GreyNoise's writeup of the Check Point campaign.

GreyNoise tracked an intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers hitting at least 22 organizations between October 17 and November 2. The actor used a compromised server as an operational relay, staging stolen firewall databases and internal CA files there.

By early November, other threat actors were scanning the relay. The actor ran a check for CVE-2026-98432, a Linux IPv4 use-after-free, then used nftables to drop the packet types that trigger it. Per GreyNoise: 'This allowed the actor to protect their hop from others engaging in future exploitation of the bug.'

Defender takeaway: attacker infrastructure gets patch hygiene too, and that shows up on your side. Unexpected nftables rules on a server nobody should be tuning, or an entry in /etc/ld.so.preload, are worth alerting on. The victims here only got identified because the actor's automation failed and shipped error output back to the hop.

Злоумышленники использовали многочисленные уязвимости для взлома двух десятков серверов управления Check Point Security в рамках продолжающейся кампании, направленной на 22 организации.

Активность выявила GreyNoise, отметившая, что она напоминает операции кибершпионажа, хотя мотивы злоумышленника окончательно установить не удалось.

Исследователи отслеживают активность под номером GT13 и подтвердили, что она продолжалась с 17 октября по 2 ноября, после чего их наблюдение прекратилось.

Однако, учитывая постоянный доступ злоумышленника к устройствам Check Point, они считают, что кампания остается активной.

По данным GreyNoise, 22 организации-жертвы расположены в 17 странах, среди которых госучреждения, поставщики финансовых услуг, а также компании энергетического, транспортного, горнодобывающего и производственного секторов.

Атаки были совершены с 99 IP, которые, судя по всему, принадлежат скомпрометированным устройствам Check Point и выходным узлам ExpressVPN.

Файловый HTTP-сервер Rejetto, скомпрометированный с помощью CVE-2026-61500, использовался в качестве оперативного ретранслятора для управления вторжениями и сбора украденных данных из скомпрометированных сред.

GreyNoise пока не смогла установить, когда и как были взломаны серверы Check Point, но зафиксировала использование CVE-2026-16232 на этапах после взлома.

Уязвимость связана с обходом аутентификации в Check Point SmartConsole, которая позволяет злоумышленникам получить токен для входа в приложение и пройти аутентификацию с правами администратора.

В свою очередь, Check Point предупредила о ней еще в июле, обозначив ее как активно используемую 0-day.

Исследователи также зафиксировали попытки использования CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole) и CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF).

26 октября злоумышленник провел операцию по массовому управлению сертификатами на всех 24 скомпрометированных серверах Check Point, которая завершилась неудачей, но зато помогла GreyNoise идентифицировать жертв.

Исследователи пришли к выводу, что GT13 использовала инструмент нападения на основе ИИ, основываясь на поведении, наблюдаемой автоматизации и специально разработанных инструментах, однако использование ИИ в этой кампании остается неподтвержденным.

Учитывая, что кампания все еще может быть активной, GreyNoise поделилась IOCs, которые могут помочь выявить дополнительные вторжения или заблокировать будущие попытки.

Представители Check Point заявляют, что им известно о действиях, описанных в отчете GreyNoise.

По их данным, злоумышленники использовали CVE-2026-16232, позволяющую обойти аутентификацию SmartConsole, о которой Check Point публично сообщила в июле 2026 года, отметив, что эксплуатация уже наблюдалась в реальных условиях.

Таким образом, эта уязвимость и доступные средства защиты не являются новыми. Злоумышленники также использовали адаптированный общедоступный модуль Metasploit для CVE-2026-16232, поэтому метод эксплуатации уже был известен ранее.

В общем, будем следить.

A worm called WeWorm spreads through WeChat with no action from the victim, moving between current iOS and Android devices.

Zero-click bugs in messaging apps are treated as rare, bespoke findings, because reaching code that runs before a user taps anything means auditing a narrow slice of a huge application. That assumption shapes how vendors prioritize the work.

The speakers argue the assumption no longer holds. With the right tooling, LLMs can enumerate remotely reachable attack surface across messaging apps then audit it automatically.

Three case studies carry the argument: WeWorm, a WhatsApp zero-click affecting Samsung devices only, along with a nearly universal iOS one-click.

In their [un]prompted 2026 talk, "0-Click Remote Exploits in an AI World," on Tuesday, October 27 at 4:45 p.m. on Stage 1, Bruce Dang and Anna Groza present the tooling along with what changes once this research is cheap to automate.

Speakers:

Bruce Dang, Calif (presenter) Anna Groza, Security Researcher, Calif (presenter)

The session closes on trust boundaries: where the assumptions behind messaging app security break down, along with what platform vendors can do to shrink remotely exposed attack surface first.

Calif published the WeWorm write-up in September 2026, credited to Calif Research rather than to individual authors. It describes memory corruption in WeChat's VoIP stack giving full account control within seconds, without the victim answering the call. Calif's OEMpocalypse research supplies the next stage, taking an unprivileged Android app to root across Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo and OnePlus flagships.

The canonical published analysis of this bug class remains Google Project Zero's teardown of NSO Group's FORCEDENTRY iMessage exploit. For WhatsApp specifically, the in-the-wild chain built on CVE-2025-55177 with Apple's CVE-2025-43300 was analyzed at 39C3 by Zhongrui Li, Yizhe Zhuang and Kira Chen, who are not connected to this talk.

Bruce Dang is listed under Leadership at Calif, a company of roughly 60 people across five continents whose team includes Thai Duong, An Trinh, Michal Zalewski and Dion Blazakis. He began at the Microsoft Security Response Center, where he analyzed Stuxnet, then spent years at Apple.

He co-presented "Adventures in analyzing Stuxnet" with Peter Ferrie at 27C3 in December 2010, a first-hand account of identifying then triaging the Stuxnet vulnerabilities. He is lead author of Practical Reverse Engineering, published by Wiley in 2014 with Alexandre Gazet, Elias Bachaalany and Sebastien Josse.

At REcon 2011 he co-presented with Rolf Rolles and Tavis Ormandy on decompiling kernel drivers. He gave "Methods for analyzing malicious Office documents" at REcon 2008, along with teaching REcon's Windows kernel rootkits training.

Активность выявила GreyNoise, отметившая, что она напоминает операции кибершпионажа, хотя мотивы злоумышленника окончательно установить не удалось.

Исследователи отслеживают активность под номером GT13 и подтвердили, что она продолжалась с 17 октября по 2 ноября, после чего их наблюдение прекратилось.

Однако, учитывая постоянный доступ злоумышленника к устройствам Check Point, они считают, что кампания остается активной.

По данным GreyNoise, 22 организации-жертвы расположены в 17 странах, среди которых госучреждения, поставщики финансовых услуг, а также компании энергетического, транспортного, горнодобывающего и производственного секторов.

Атаки были совершены с 99 IP, которые, судя по всему, принадлежат скомпрометированным устройствам Check Point и выходным узлам ExpressVPN.

Файловый HTTP-сервер Rejetto, скомпрометированный с помощью CVE-2026-61500, использовался в качестве оперативного ретранслятора для управления вторжениями и сбора украденных данных из скомпрометированных сред.

Уязвимость связана с обходом аутентификации в Check Point SmartConsole, которая позволяет злоумышленникам получить токен для входа в приложение и пройти аутентификацию с правами администратора.

В свою очередь, Check Point предупредила о ней еще в июле, обозначив ее как активно используемую 0-day.

Исследователи также зафиксировали попытки использования CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole) и CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF).

26 октября злоумышленник провел операцию по массовому управлению сертификатами на всех 24 скомпрометированных серверах Check Point, которая завершилась неудачей, но зато помогла GreyNoise идентифицировать жертв.

Исследователи пришли к выводу, что GT13 использовала инструмент нападения на основе ИИ, основываясь на поведении, наблюдаемой автоматизации и специально разработанных инструментах, однако использование ИИ в этой кампании остается неподтвержденным.

Учитывая, что кампания все еще может быть активной, GreyNoise поделилась IOCs, которые могут помочь выявить дополнительные вторжения или заблокировать будущие попытки.

Представители Check Point заявляют, что им известно о действиях, описанных в отчете GreyNoise.

По их данным, злоумышленники использовали CVE-2026-16232, позволяющую обойти аутентификацию SmartConsole, о которой Check Point публично сообщила в июле 2026 года, отметив, что эксплуатация уже наблюдалась в реальных условиях.

Таким образом, эта уязвимость и доступные средства защиты не являются новыми. Злоумышленники также использовали адаптированный общедоступный модуль Metasploit для CVE-2026-16232, поэтому метод эксплуатации уже был известен ранее.

В общем, будем следить.

Tendril is a Windows persistence toolkit implemented as a .NET 4.0 C# assembly, a unified Beacon Object File (BOF), and integrations for Mythic and Cobalt Strike. Its C# version contains 22 modules, while the BOF supports 14 modules through a shared dispatch function. The documented operations include installing or checking persistence mechanisms such as COM hijacking, ghost scheduled tasks, IFEO injection, screensaver persistence, AppInit DLLs, Winlogon helpers, accessibility features, Netsh helpers, Userinit/MPR persistence, port monitors, Security Support Providers (SSPs), time provider DLLs, and Active Setup entries.

The command interface generally accepts a module, an action such as `install` or `check`, and module-specific arguments, including file paths, registry hives, process names, and identifiers. The Mythic integration supports Apollo and EmeraldStrike. For BOF execution, Mythic requires registering the BOF and optionally its JSON schema; the Cobalt Strike integration uses an Aggressor script. The BOF can be built on Windows or Linux-compatible environments using the supplied build scripts and MinGW or MSYS2. Adding a module requires implementing its BOF function and updating the dispatch logic and module identifiers in the related integrations.

The persistence methods correspond to established Windows mechanisms. The report cites ghost scheduled tasks created by deleting or altering security descriptors in TaskCache, a technique associated with Tarrask, and references research on COM hijacking, DLL proxying, port-monitor persistence, SSPs, time providers, Active Setup, IFEO, and accessibility features. These mechanisms can enable execution at logon, during service or system activity, or when specific applications or components are launched. The report also lists broader research on other persistence and evasion methods, but does not describe their implementation as Tendril modules.

19 years of BitLocker lockout just collapsed to 20 days because of a $1 motherboard flash chip.

Firmware TPMs on modern laptops store failed PIN counts on external SPI flash. TPM 2.0 Dictionary Attack Protection enforces a 32-try limit followed by one guess every 10 minutes, relying on a JEDEC counter called RPMC inside that flash chip to stop state rollbacks.

 At ACM CCS 2026, researchers broke that lock on both sides.
On Winbond RPMC flash (25R and 74M chips), a 1-second voltage glitch leaks the HMAC signing key straight out of the chip. Any laptop using that flash, Intel or AMD, now accepts forged counter values and rolls back its failed-attempt state.

On AMD fTPM (CVE-2026-43613), the firmware skips verifying whether the counter ever incremented. A custom interposer sitting between the CPU and SPI flash blocks counter updates with zero glitching.

 Measured worst-case brute-force results on locked laptops:
  * 4-digit Windows Hello PIN: 69 days down to 40 hours
  * 6-digit BitLocker startup PIN: 19 years down to 20 days

Winbond has no patch timeline because fixing the leak takes new silicon. AMD published AMD-SB-7079 with firmware fixes rolling out from November 2026 through February 2027.

Researchers used a flash-chip interposer to bypass TPM lockout and guess Hello and BitLocker PINs in lab tests; AMD tracks CVE-2026-43613 (CVSS 5.1). Check devices for tampering; lengthen PINs.

Your PC has a mechanism that remembers every incorrect PIN attempt and eventually locks you out

Researchers at TU Berlin found a way to make that mechanism forget

Their attack, called Hello Again, targets the Replay Protected Monotonic Counters (RPMC) used to protect security state stored in motherboard flash memory

The TPM relies on this state to remember failed authentication attempts and prevent brute-force guessing

The researchers found two ways to undermine that protection:

On affected AMD systems, they intercepted communication between the processor and flash chip, suppressing counter updates while making the processor believe they succeeded
On systems using vulnerable Winbond flash chips, voltage glitching exposed a cryptographic key that allowed the researchers to forge counter values

With the lockout state repeatedly reset, they could automate PIN guesses without the normal security delays

Their laboratory demonstrations included:

A four-digit Windows Hello PIN found in 57 minutes, with a worst-case estimated search time of 40 hours instead of 69 days
A six-digit BitLocker startup PIN found in under seven minutes, with a worst-case estimate of 20 days instead of 19 years

The attack required physical access, specialised hardware and vulnerable hardware configurations

It also affects different platforms for different reasons

AMD assigned its firmware issue CVE-2026-43613 and is planning firmware fixes extending into February 2027

Intel says the research did not demonstrate a vulnerability in Intel components; the tested Intel system depended on a flaw in its third-party Winbond flash chip

For now, researchers recommend using longer PINs, adding at least two digits where possible

The deeper security lesson is that a PIN's strength depends not only on how difficult it is to guess, but also on whether the hardware enforcing guess limits can be trusted

The report describes misuse of ARTEX, an LLM-powered penetration-testing framework, across several campaigns. Reported activity includes attacks against South Korean financial organizations, Japanese companies, IT and software vendors, and financial-sector targets. The operators remain unknown in the Korean and Japanese cases; the report treats them as separate intrusions and does not infer shared attribution from overlapping infrastructure. Storm-0940 activity involved password spraying and abuse of ConnectWise Cloud Backup-related access. Storm-3358 activity involved financial-sector targeting and infrastructure associated with WISP. Other reported tools include vshell and AdaptixC2.

Common behaviors include rapid reconnaissance of web and API surfaces; enumeration of distinct customer or application records; probing authentication, SSO, OAuth, and application endpoints; and password spraying with rotating user agents. Other patterns include repeated requests with altered headers or tokens, SSRF attempts using redirecting URLs to reach internal or metadata addresses, and downloading exposed configuration or backup files. Cloud activity includes exposed-secret use, service-principal sign-ins, OAuth credential addition, and credential discovery across AWS services. The report also describes upload-then-execute behavior and self-correcting API retries, including retries after HTTP 422 responses.

The detection approach prioritizes behavior over framework-specific strings, which can be changed or generated by the model. Proposed rules correlate sequences such as multiple distinct reconnaissance requests within a short window, high-volume record access, and file uploads followed by execution. ARTEX-specific headers, user agents, webshell keys, response markers, domains, and IP addresses are treated as supporting indicators; shared infrastructure and generic user agents require caution. Reported Windows artifacts include files named in an intent-ID/purpose/extension format and paths under `C:\Windows\Temp` or `C:\ProgramData`; these are described as renameable indicators rather than durable detections.

The report recommends correlating network telemetry with identity and cloud logs. Zeek can identify indicators and behavioral sequences in DNS, connection, and decrypted HTTP data, while cloud and identity rules cover activity not visible at the network perimeter. IP-based indicators may be reassigned or shared, so the report advises against blocking them automatically; some generic indicators are enrichment-only. It also notes a known gap: password spraying distributed across many source IPs can evade per-IP thresholds.

GreyNoise observed an intrusion campaign attributed to the untracked actor GT13 against Check Point Security Management Servers from October 17 to November 2, 2026. At least 22 organizations across multiple regions and sectors were affected. The actor used Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and custom Python scripts for exploitation, internal reconnaissance, credential discovery, privilege escalation attempts, and lateral movement.

The actor first compromised an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500. By collecting session cookies generated through HFS’s `loginSrp1` endpoint, they reconstructed the V8 pseudorandom-number generator state, recovered the signing key, and forged an administrator cookie. The cookie allowed access from a different IP address. The compromised server was then prepared as an operational relay: the actor attempted to install malware, created an unauthenticated HTTP file-upload service, and configured Chisel as a reverse proxy.

From this relay, GT13 accessed Check Point environments and used a script for CVE-2026-16232, an authentication bypass that enables command execution through SmartConsole. The actor launched more than 100 management tasks, attempted to copy firewall databases and Internal CA files, and generated a certificate named `pivot.p12`. They also attempted to unload security policies, which could disable firewalls, and probed systems including Citrix NetScaler, Ivanti Connect Secure, VMware vCenter, Microsoft Exchange, Oracle TNS, and domain controllers. Scripts performed broad port scanning and SSH credential attempts using victim-themed usernames and passwords.

Other vulnerabilities the actor used or attempted to exploit included CVE-2025-5777, CVE-2024-21893, CVE-2026-41089, and CVE-2026-98432. On the relay, GT13 checked for the Linux IPv4 use-after-free vulnerability CVE-2026-98432 and attempted to mitigate it with `nftables` rules dropping IPv4 packets containing IP options.

GreyNoise tracks GT13, a suspected AI-enabled campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers, hitting at least 22 orgs worldwide and using a compromised HFS server as a relay.

- Scope: confirmed attack activity ran Oct 17 to Nov 2, 2026, across financial services, energy, government, transportation, mining, engineering, and manufacturing. GreyNoise does not attribute GT13 to any tracked group or assess motive. The actor used 99 IPs, all ExpressVPN egress or compromised Check Point devices, over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files. The actor already had Check Point access before the HFS compromise, and how they got it is unknown. Persistent access suggests the campaign is ongoing.

- Relay build: on 2026-10-02 the actor hit Rejetto HFS with CVE-2026-61500. Repeated POSTs to loginSrp1 leaked sid values from Math.random(), enough to rebuild V8 PRNG state, recover the cookie signing key, and forge an admin session. The forged cookie carried allow_session_ip_change:true, so it worked from any VPN exit. The actor then used HFS middleware hooks to append an SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys. A check-in ran "uname -a; df -h / | tail -1; whoami". An attempted ZULT Linux implant download via server_code from newpayapp[.]com (registered 2026-03-13) failed. The actor came back over SSH the next day.

- Hop tradecraft: a script at /root/exfil/srv_post2_<redacted>.py stood up an unauthenticated HTTP server for uploads. The actor installed Nmap and Chisel, ran a Chisel server as a reverse proxy, and ran Chisel in client mode on a Victim A asset. Bulk results from 24 compromised Check Point servers landed in /root/exfil/pc_<victim IP>.txt. Each server pushed its file via scp, so each holds the SSH private key matching the key planted on the hop.

- Check Point abuse: the actor used exploit[.]py, a purported adaptation of the Metasploit module for CVE-2026-16232 (SmartConsole auth bypass to Run Script), to launch over 100 management tasks. These copied the firewall database and Internal CA, minted a certificate (pivot.p12), and unloaded security policies, which would disable the firewall. pull_<id>.py chained exploit_socks.py to harvest credentials, CA files, and firewall config through one compromised device to the hop. One error output showed a preload error for /usr/lib/.libproc.so registered in /etc/ld.so.preload, which may indicate an implant.

- Internal ops: the actor used Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and at least 30 Python scripts, including spray_portal.py, comb[.]py, ssh_comb.py, and ssh_spray.py with victim-themed passwords. Exploit attempts hit Netlogon CVE-2020-1472, Citrix CVE-2023-4966, Ivanti CVE-2024-21893, Exchange CVE-2021-26855/34473, and vCenter CVE-2021-21972/CVE-2023-34048. On 2026-11-02 the actor even tried to patch its own hop for CVE-2026-98432 with nftables rules dropping IPv4 packets with IP options, to keep rivals out.

Takeaway: on Check Point management servers, check /etc/ld.so.preload and /usr/lib/.libproc.so, review Run Script and management task history for bulk certificate or policy-unload actions, and look for pivot.p12, unexpected SSH private keys, and scp uploads to unknown hosts. On any HFS host, hunt for loginSrp1 POST bursts, forged-cookie admin requests, command hooks, unexpected authorized_keys entries, and /root/exfil. Preserve the nftables rules too. The report has excerpts of the actor's scripts but no IOC table.

Due to checking write permissions using the real user ID and subsequently opening the file using the effective user ID, a local unprivileged attacker can atomically replace the target path with a symbolic link pointing to an arbitrary system file. Successfully exploiting this race condition allows the attacker to write to arbitrary files with root privileges, leading to local privilege escalation



This issue was fixed in version 5.0.2.

This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that at least one prior comment from the attacker's email address has been manually approved, which under WordPress's default comment previously approved=1 setting causes subsequent comments from that address to be auto-approved without moderation.

The Pixeline’s Email Protector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the malicious comment to pass the site's moderation queue, which WordPress enforces for first-time commenters by default but which does not re-sanitize stored comment content.

products: Taskbuilder – Project Management & Task Management Tool With Kanban Board
vulnerabilities.description: The Taskbuilder – Project Management & Task Management Tool With Kanban Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'display name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.0.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload fires specifically when an authenticated user with access to the Tasks admin panel applies the 'Created By' filter with the attacker-controlled user selected. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

products: Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert Webp & Avif | Cdn & Lazy Load | Image Optimization
vulnerabilities.description: The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that iframe lazy-loading is enabled (the default on new Optimole-connected installs), that the target post contains at least one iframe with fallback text, and that the attacker has had at least one prior comment approved so WordPress's default "Comment author must have a previously approved comment" setting auto-approves subsequent malicious comments.

The LA-Studio Element Kit for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'actions[].data.settings.triggers.scrolling to selector' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The elementor ajax nonce required to reach the handler is printed in elementorCommonConfig on every wp-admin page, making it trivially obtainable by any logged-in Subscriber via /wp-admin/profile.php; although Elementor's attribute escaping is applied at render time, the stored selector value is subsequently passed to jQuery() by the popup frontend script, which re-parses strings beginning with '<' as HTML, bypassing the escaping.

The Postie plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'email HTML body' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.91 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable when the processing request runs under a user holding the unfiltered html capability — either because 'Force User Login' is enabled and Postie switches to the default poster, or because an administrator manually triggers the fetch — causing wp filter post kses to be stripped from content save pre and the attribute-breakout markup to be stored verbatim by wp insert post().

The Asset CleanUp Pro: Page Speed Booster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to blind SQL Injection via 'author name' URL segment (author archive rewrite capture) in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.8.1 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

The Fluent Forms – Customizable Contact Forms, Survey, Quiz, & Conversational Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Account Pre-Hijacking via Unverified Identifier in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.15. The vulnerability exists because the `PaymentHandler::maybeAssignTransactions()` function, registered on the `user register` hook at priority 99, resolves the lookup email solely from the newly created user record via the `user email` parameter with no prior verification that the registrant actually controls that address, then bulk-updates all guest transactions and submissions in `wp fluentform transactions` and `wp fluentform submissions` whose `payer email` matches and whose `user id` is NULL to assign ownership to the attacker's new account. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to pre-hijack a victim's prior guest payment history — reading their payment receipts and cancelling their active subscriptions via the `[fluentform payments]` shortcode and the `wp ajax fluentform user payment endpoints` `cancel transaction` route — by simply registering an account under the victim's email address before the legitimate owner does. Exploitation requires that the WordPress site has open user registration enabled and that the targeted victim previously submitted at least one payment as a guest under their email address.

The UsersWP – Front-end login form, User Registration, User Profile & Members Directory plugin for WP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the '<htmlvar name> of any editor-type Account field (e.g. about work)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.83 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured at least one editor-type Account field with public visibility and directory display enabled, as no such field exists in a default installation.

products: The Rss Aggregator By Feedzy – Feed To Post
vulnerabilities.description: The RSS Aggregator by Feedzy – Feed to Post, Autoblogging, News & YouTube Video Feeds Aggregator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in versions up to, and including, 5.2.17 due to insufficient restriction on the wp kses allowed html filter callback. The feedzy wp kses allowed html() method is registered on wp kses allowed html with the loader's default accepted args=1, so the callback never receives the context-name argument and unconditionally adds <iframe> (with arbitrary src, width, height, frameborder, allowfullscreen and data-* attributes) to the allowed-tag array for every context — including pre comment content, which WordPress uses to sanitize comment bodies submitted by users without the unfiltered html capability. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The PDF Invoices & Packing Slips for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing address.first name / company / address 1 / address 2 / city' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the E-Documents feature to be enabled with a UBL PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format, as that setting is disabled by default and controls whether the vulnerable meta box is registered and rendered.

products: Easy Social Share Buttons For Wordpress
vulnerabilities.description: The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'position' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is stored via the unauthenticated wp ajax nopriv ESSB stat log AJAX action, which performs no nonce or capability check, and executes when the attacker-controlled position value is rendered verbatim into a double-quoted HTML data-* attribute where the unescaped quote allows attribute breakout.

products: Easy Form Builder By Whitestudio – Drag & Drop Form Builder
vulnerabilities.description: The Easy Form Builder by WhiteStudio – Drag & Drop Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via esign 'value' Field via Cross-Type 'r matrix' Poisoning in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation is possible without authentication because the REST endpoint /wp-json/Emsfb/v1/forms/message/add is guarded only by a wp rest nonce freely obtainable by any visitor loading the public-facing form page via efb var.nonce.

The BuddyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<form field slug>[] (array-valued post field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.10 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the BuddyForms form to have public submission enabled, which allows unauthenticated visitors to submit forms; the wpnonce required by the form handler is printed in the public form HTML and is therefore accessible to any visitor, providing no meaningful authorization barrier.

The SlimStat Analytics – Real-Time Stats, Heatmaps & Ecommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP USER AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the non-default 'Show user agent' (slimstat options[show complete user agent tooltip]) setting to be enabled, which causes the raw stored User-Agent value to be used as the tooltip title instead of a sanitized browser name.

A maliciously modified field in the locally stored JSON description for an update made available by Autodesk, when processed by Autodesk Access, can cause attacker-controlled HTML content to be executed in another user's session. A local, authenticated malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of another user if that user interacts with an injected link, resulting in privilege escalation.

products: Xagio Seo & Aeo – Ai Seo For Google Rankings & Ai Visibility
vulnerabilities.description: The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.54 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution of the injected script requires an administrator to use the plugin's own "Add 301 Redirect" workflow on the attacker's logged 404 row, which causes the entity-laundered double quote to be written into the redirects table and subsequently rendered unescaped in the administrator's browser. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

products: Geodirectory – Wp Business Directory Plugin/Classified Listings Directory
vulnerabilities.description: The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'stype' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.208 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. This is possible because the plugin's mu-plugin companion (copied automatically on install when the default 'Enable Fast AJAX' option is on) defines DOING AJAX on any front-end request carrying gd-ajax=1, and an unconditional branch in geodir get current posttype() restores the attacker-controlled stype value after the allow-list check clears it, allowing the tainted value to reach the SQL sink without any preparation.

The SlimStat Analytics plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'filter array' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a non-default administrator configuration in which the can view whitelist contains at least one username of which the attacker's login is a substring (e.g., can view set to 'trustedreporter' while the attacker's login is 'report'), and the stored payload only fires when an administrator subsequently opens the Saved Filters dialog.

products: The Nextmove Lite – Thank You Page For Woocommerce
vulnerabilities.description: The NextMove Lite – Thank You Page for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing address.email' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.24.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected script fires without any victim interaction because the builder page's JavaScript calls $(".preview order id").trigger("change") on page load, immediately executing any attribute-injected event handler.

products: The Email Encoder – Protect Email Addresses/Phone Numbers
vulnerabilities.description: The Email Encoder – Protect Email Addresses and Phone Numbers plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a site administrator to have enabled the plugin's non-default "Protect custom href attributes" setting (e.g. configured to 'tel'), and injected comments must pass standard WordPress moderation before the script executes for visiting users.

The PDF Invoices & Packing Slips for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing address.address 1' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires the E-Documents feature to be enabled with a document format selected, as this is what causes the vulnerable meta box to be rendered on the order edit screen.

The GD bbPress Tools plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'signature' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The crafted signature payload is stored verbatim in user meta and fires when an Administrator views the attacker's topic on the Edit Topic admin screen.

The Product Input Fields for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.0 via the process file input field function. This is due to missing file type validation in the process file input field function, which accepts the client-supplied multipart Content-Type header as the sole type gate and writes the uploaded file to the unprotected pif temp directory using the verbatim client-supplied filename. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured at least one product with a File-type Product Input Field with the "Show thumbnail" option enabled, which is a standard use of the feature; additionally, the pif temp/ upload directory is created without .htaccess or index.php restrictions, leaving written files directly web-accessible and executable on default Apache/mod php configurations.

The WP Statistics – Simple, privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 14.16.19 via the 'tab' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The exploitability of this vulnerability depends on the Minimum Role to View Statistics setting; when set to a low-privilege role such as Subscriber (read capability), unauthenticated-equivalent access is effectively granted to any registered user, while the default Administrator setting limits exposure to higher-privileged accounts.
